`re/src/ac1_mission.c`:

```c
/* ac1_mission.c — behavioral reference model of the AC1 mission runtime.
 * Portable C99. See ac1_mission.h and docs/MISSION_STATE_MACHINE.md.
 *
 * Confidence labels follow the docs: CONFIRMED = disasm/byte-verified or
 * live-observed; HYPOTHESIS = inferred. Open points cite docs/LIVE_CHECKLIST.md. */
#include "ac1_mission.h"
#include <string.h>

static uint16_t rd16(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint16_t)(p[0] | (p[1] << 8)); }
static int16_t  rds16(const uint8_t *p) { return (int16_t)rd16(p); }
static uint32_t rd32(const uint8_t *p) {
    return (uint32_t)p[0] | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 8) |
           ((uint32_t)p[2] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[3] << 24);
}
static void wr16(uint8_t *p, uint16_t v) { p[0] = (uint8_t)v; p[1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); }

/* ========================================================================= */
/* DATA — chunk stream (FUN_8004F508 walk)  CONFIRMED                        */
/* ========================================================================= */
void ac1_chunk_begin(ac1_chunk_iter *it, const uint8_t *stream, size_t size) {
    it->buf = stream; it->size = size; it->off = 0; it->idx = 0;
}

int ac1_chunk_next(ac1_chunk_iter *it, unsigned *idx, const uint8_t **payload,
                   uint32_t *len) {
    if (!it->buf || it->off + 4 > it->size) return 0;
    uint32_t ln = rd32(it->buf + it->off);
    /* `len = u32@s1; handler(s1+4); s1 += len+4` — a zero or out-of-range
     * length is the terminator (tools/mission/mission_parse.walk_chunks). */
    if (ln == 0 || it->off + 4 + ln > it->size) return 0;
    if (idx) *idx = it->idx;
    if (payload) *payload = it->buf + it->off + 4;
    if (len) *len = ln;
    it->off += 4 + ln;
    it->idx++;
    return 1;
}

int ac1_chunk_find(const uint8_t *stream, size_t size, unsigned want,
                   const uint8_t **payload, uint32_t *len) {
    ac1_chunk_iter it; unsigned idx; const uint8_t *p; uint32_t ln;
    ac1_chunk_begin(&it, stream, size);
    while (ac1_chunk_next(&it, &idx, &p, &ln)) {
        if (idx == want) { if (payload) *payload = p; if (len) *len = ln; return 1; }
        if (idx > want) break;
    }
    return 0;
}

/* ========================================================================= */
/* DATA — spawn table + marshal                                              */
/* ========================================================================= */
int ac1_spawn_get(const uint8_t *chunk12, uint32_t len, unsigned i, ac1_spawn_rec *out) {
    if (i >= AC1_SPAWN_COUNT || (size_t)(i + 1) * AC1_SPAWN_REC_LEN > len) return 0;
    const uint8_t *p = chunk12 + (size_t)i * AC1_SPAWN_REC_LEN;
    for (int k = 0; k < 20; k++) out->hw[k] = rds16(p + 2 * k);
    return 1;
}

int ac1_spawn_is_empty(const ac1_spawn_rec *r) {
    /* mission_parse.dump_spawns: block == -1 and zero position */
    return r->hw[3] == -1 && r->hw[0] == 0 && r->hw[1] == 0 && r->hw[2] == 0;
}

/* FUN_80073B74 (0x80073B74), CONFIRMED structure:
 *   rec[+0x00] = 0 (status; runtime-set)
 *   rec[+0x04 + 2K] = hwK, K = 0..19            (flat reshape, stride 40 -> 44)
 *   rec[+0x02] = rec[+0x1A]  (= hw11, the HP seed; template +0x02 = "current HP")
 * docs/MISSION_SYSTEM.md §2 once recorded the derived copy as +0x00 = +0x18 —
 * the current decompile (DESTRUCTIBLE_OBJECTS.md "Record layout",
 * MISSION_STAGES.md Part 2) says +0x02 = +0x1A; LIVE_CHECKLIST S-5 seals it. */
void ac1_spawn_marshal(const ac1_spawn_rec *r, uint8_t out[AC1_TEMPLATE_LEN]) {
    memset(out, 0, AC1_TEMPLATE_LEN);
    for (int k = 0; k < 20; k++) wr16(out + 4 + 2 * k, (uint16_t)r->hw[k]);
    wr16(out + 2, rd16(out + 0x1A));
}

/* ========================================================================= */
/* DATA — secondary VM blob  (MISSION_SCRIPT_VM.md, byte-verified)           */
/* ========================================================================= */
static const ac1_vmop VMOPS[] = {
    { 0x0000, "copy_pos_lo",   6 },
    { 0x0002, "copy_pos_hi",   6 },
    { 0x0008, "spawn_at8",     6 },
    { 0x0009, "spawn_at9",     6 },
    { 0x000A, "init_unit",     12 },
    { 0x000B, "subcall_b320",  0 },
    { 0x000E, "mark_lerp",     14 },
    { 0x000F, "op_f",          -1 },   /* u16 cnt, then cnt*4 bytes */
    { 0x1000, "sel_actor",     2 },
    { 0x1001, "set_xyz",       6 },
    { 0x1002, "set_xyz2",      6 },
    { 0x1003, "spawn_group",   2 },
    { 0x1004, "play_sound",    2 },
    { 0x1005, "flag_all",      0 },
    { 0x1006, "clear_targets", 0 },
    { 0x1007, "call_db18",     2 },
    { 0x1008, "set_obj_flag",  6 },
    { 0x1009, "spawn_marker",  6 },
    { 0x100A, "set_result",    2 },
    { 0x100B, "set_obj_word",  4 },
    { 0x100C, "despawn_group", 2 },
    { 0xFFF0, "set_loop",      2 },
    { 0xFFFF, "END",           0 },
};
static const ac1_vmop VMOP_NOOP = { 0, "noop", 0 };

const ac1_vmop *ac1_vm_lookup(uint16_t op) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof VMOPS / sizeof VMOPS[0]; i++)
        if (VMOPS[i].op == op) return &VMOPS[i];
    return &VMOP_NOOP;   /* reserved words are 0-operand silent no-ops in v1.1 */
}

size_t ac1_vm_oplen(const uint8_t *blob, size_t size, size_t pc) {
    if (pc + 2 > size) return 0;
    uint16_t op = rd16(blob + pc);
    size_t total;
    if (op == AC1_VMOP_OP_F) {
        if (pc + 4 > size) return 0;
        total = 4 + (size_t)rd16(blob + pc + 2) * 4;
    } else {
        total = 2 + (size_t)ac1_vm_lookup(op)->oplen;
    }
    return (pc + total <= size) ? total : 0;
}

unsigned ac1_vm_nsets(const uint8_t *blob, size_t size) {
    if (size < 2) return 0;
    return rd16(blob) / 2;
}

int ac1_vm_set_get(const uint8_t *blob, size_t size, unsigned s, ac1_vm_set *out) {
    unsigned n = ac1_vm_nsets(blob, size);
    if (s >= n || (size_t)(2 * s + 2) > size) return 0;
    memset(out, 0, sizeof *out);
    out->offset = rd16(blob + 2 * s);
    /* A set_offset inside the offset table itself (e.g. 0) or past the blob is
     * a placeholder slot (seen in 019.bin); the loader never derefs it because
     * no shipped mission requests that index. Mirror mission_script.parse. */
    if (out->offset < n * 2 || (size_t)out->offset + 6 > size) { out->sentinel = 1; return 1; }
    out->flags = rd16(blob + out->offset);
    out->count = rd16(blob + out->offset + 2);
    out->extra = rd16(blob + out->offset + 4);
    return 1;
}

uint16_t ac1_vm_thread_offset(const uint8_t *blob, size_t size, const ac1_vm_set *s, unsigned t) {
    if (s->sentinel || t >= s->count) return 0;
    size_t at = (size_t)s->offset + 6 + 2 * t;
    if (at + 2 > size) return 0;
    return rd16(blob + at);
}

int ac1_vm_thread_walk(const uint8_t *blob, size_t size, uint16_t toff,
                       unsigned *nops, size_t *nbytes) {
    size_t pc = (size_t)toff + 2;   /* thread_hdr, then PC starts at +2 */
    unsigned n = 0;
    if ((size_t)toff + 2 > size) return 0;
    for (unsigned guard = 0; guard < 4096; guard++) {
        size_t ln = ac1_vm_oplen(blob, size, pc);
        if (ln == 0) return 0;
        uint16_t op = rd16(blob + pc);
        n++; pc += ln;
        if (op == AC1_VMOP_END) {
            if (nops) *nops = n;
            if (nbytes) *nbytes = pc - toff;
            return 1;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

/* ========================================================================= */
/* RUNTIME — shared lifecycle                                                */
/* ========================================================================= */
static void hook_sound(ac1_mission *m, int id) {
    if (m->hooks.sound) m->hooks.sound(m->hooks.user, id);
}

/* FUN_8004F508 prologue (CONFIRMED): init the control block, store the mission
 * number, zero the displayed timer (0x8004F9FC). Init values 128/0/64 for
 * +0x12/+0x14/+0x16 are recorded as "partial" in MISSION_SYSTEM.md §5. */
void ac1_mission_init(ac1_mission *m, uint8_t number, const ac1_objobj *obj,
                      const ac1_mission_hooks *hooks) {
    memset(m, 0, sizeof *m);
    m->mission_number = number;
    m->f52e = 128; m->f530 = 0; m->f532 = 64;
    m->obj = obj;
    if (hooks) m->hooks = *hooks;
}

/* FUN_8004C318(a0) (CONFIRMED by disasm + live):
 *   "Writes a0 directly into 0x8019F524, and if 0x8019F528 == 0 sets it to 100."
 * A direct store means a later set_result() would drop bits set in between
 * (e.g. the 0x400 event bit) — yet the live exit read 0x480 = 0x80 | 0x400.
 * Store-vs-OR is LIVE_CHECKLIST MIS-15; the model follows the disasm (store). */
void ac1_mission_set_result(ac1_mission *m, uint32_t flags) {
    m->flags = flags;
    if (m->end_counter == 0) m->end_counter = AC1_MIS_END_FADE_FRAMES;
}

/* FUN_8008A80C (CONFIRMED): progress counter 0x8009079C, range-checked < 37. */
void ac1_mission_objective_step(ac1_mission *m) {
    if (m->progress > AC1_MIS_PROGRESS_TERMINAL) return;      /* out of range: ignored */
    if (m->progress == AC1_MIS_PROGRESS_TERMINAL) {
        m->end_anim = 0;
        m->terminal = 1;                                     /* 0x801CC80C = 1 */
        m->flags &= ~AC1_MIS_FLAG_OBJ_PENDING;
        return;
    }
    m->end_anim = 0xFFFF;                                    /* start end sequence */
    m->flags |= AC1_MIS_FLAG_OBJ_PENDING;
    if (m->progress != 0) hook_sound(m, 101);                /* FUN_800529F0(0,0,101) */
    m->progress++;
}

/* FUN_8008A8F8 (CONFIRMED): run by the driver when end_anim < 61.
 *   state == 60: special end action (DAT_80039C5D callback), clears 0x1000;
 *   else: decrement end_anim toward 0.
 * It also re-writes the flags word every frame (`lw; and ~0x1000; sw` at
 * 0x8008A938) to clear the transient timer-warn bit — the "masker" that defeats
 * a naive watchpoint (MISSION_SYSTEM.md §6). */
void ac1_mission_eventflags_tick(ac1_mission *m) {
    if (m->end_anim == AC1_MIS_END_ANIM_SPECIAL) {
        if (m->hooks.end_special) m->hooks.end_special(m->hooks.user);
    } else if (m->end_anim > 0) {
        m->end_anim--;
    }
    m->flags &= ~AC1_MIS_FLAG_TIMER_WARN;
}

/* cmd 4 (0x8008A178) / FUN_8008A778: timer = 22 * param (×22 and the frame unit
 * are HYPOTHESIS — LIVE_CHECKLIST MIS-2); type 128/256/512 -> timer struct. */
void ac1_mission_set_timer(ac1_mission *m, uint32_t param, uint16_t type) {
    m->timer = AC1_MIS_TIMER_SCALE * param;
    m->countdown_type = type;
    m->countdown = (uint16_t)(m->timer > 0xFFFF ? 0xFFFF : m->timer);
}

/* Timer tick handler (~0x8004C4F0 / caller 0x8004C5F0): on expiry
 * FUN_8004C318(0x200) = FAIL. The per-frame decrement rate of the displayed
 * timer is modelled as 1/frame (HYPOTHESIS; MIS-2). */
static void timer_tick(ac1_mission *m) {
    if (m->timer == 0) return;
    m->timer--;
    if (m->timer == 0) ac1_mission_set_result(m, AC1_MIS_FLAG_FAIL);
}

/* FUN_8008AA90: end-sequence step + screen flash; the counter armed to 100 by
 * set_result counts down and the mission exits at 0 (CONFIRMED live: ~100-frame
 * fade to the debrief). */
static void end_step(ac1_mission *m) {
    if (m->end_counter == 0) return;
    m->end_counter--;
    if (m->end_counter == 0 && !m->exited) {
        m->exited = 1;
        m->result_code = ac1_mission_exit_result(m);
        if (m->hooks.exit) m->hooks.exit(m->hooks.user, m->result_code);
    }
}

/* FUN_8008A0B0 (CONFIRMED table; jump table 0x8004C164). */
int ac1_mission_cmd(ac1_mission *m, int cmd, int arg) {
    switch (cmd) {
    case 1:  /* clear a method-table flag on a range of objects */      return 0;
    case 2:  /* FUN_8008C2FC: load secondary-VM thread set `arg` */     return 0;
    case 3:  /* FUN_8008A048: toggle group enable */                    return 0;
    case 4:  ac1_mission_set_timer(m, (uint32_t)arg, 128);              return 0;
    case 5:  ac1_mission_set_result(m, AC1_MIS_FLAG_PROGRESS);          return 0;
    case 6:  /* enable group + per-object counter (FUN_8008A080) */     return 0;
    case 7:  /* group + counter */                                      return 0;
    case 8:  /* prompt-gated success: FUN_80052A2C(99) == 1 -> 0x100.
                The prompt is a host decision here: arg != 0 means "the
                prompt returned 1" (exact trigger: LIVE_CHECKLIST MIS-3). */
             if (arg) ac1_mission_set_result(m, AC1_MIS_FLAG_SUCCESS);
             return 0;
    case 9:  if (m->obj && m->obj->event) m->obj->event(m, arg);        return 0;
    case 10: /* broadcast 0x8200+sub to a range of objects */           return 0;
    default: return -1;
    }
}

/* One mission frame of the mode-2 handler body (~0x8004C3xx): the driver
 * FUN_8008AB68 is called at 0x8004C480 (CONFIRMED order inside it), and the
 * timer-tick handler (~0x8004C4F0, FAIL call at 0x8004C5F0) runs after it in
 * the same body — so a timer that expires this frame arms the fade for the
 * NEXT frame's end step. */
void ac1_mission_frame(ac1_mission *m) {
    if (m->exited) return;
    m->frame++;
    if (m->obj && m->obj->tick) m->obj->tick(m);                      /* [*0x8019F51C+0] */
    if (m->end_anim < AC1_MIS_END_ANIM_ACTIVE_LT) ac1_mission_eventflags_tick(m);
    if (m->end_counter != 0) end_step(m);
    timer_tick(m);
}

/* 0x8004C69C (CONFIRMED): 0x100 -> 1, 0x200 -> 2, neither -> 0. The order when
 * both bits are set is not documented; success is tested first here. Note that
 * the live border-exit path commits 0x80 (cmd 5), which this table maps to 0 —
 * how the debrief distinguishes success is LIVE_CHECKLIST MIS-16. */
uint32_t ac1_mission_exit_result(const ac1_mission *m) {
    if (m->flags & AC1_MIS_FLAG_SUCCESS) return AC1_MIS_RESULT_SUCCESS;
    if (m->flags & AC1_MIS_FLAG_FAIL)    return AC1_MIS_RESULT_FAIL;
    return 0;
}

const char *ac1_mission_phase(const ac1_mission *m) {
    if (m->exited)                                  return "EXITED";
    if (m->end_counter != 0)                        return "ENDING";
    if (m->objectives_state == 3)                   return "OBJECTIVES_COMPLETE";
    if (m->terminal)                                return "TERMINAL";
    if (m->frame == 0)                              return "LOADED";
    return "RUNNING";
}

```

`re/src/ac1_mxt.c`:

```c
/* ac1_mxt.c — behavioral reference model of the AC1 MXT container + checksum.
 * Portable C99. See ac1_mxt.h and docs/MXT_LOADER.md. */
#include "ac1_mxt.h"
#include <string.h>

static uint16_t rd16(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint16_t)(p[0] | (p[1] << 8)); }
static uint32_t rd32(const uint8_t *p) {
    return (uint32_t)p[0] | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 8) |
           ((uint32_t)p[2] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[3] << 24);
}

/* Heuristic mirror of tools/extract/extract_t.py: count-first archives store the entry
 * count in u16[0] with offsets beginning at u16[1] (FDAT.T, MENU_TIM.T);
 * offset-first store offset[0]==1 in u16[0]. */
static ac1_toc_kind detect_kind(const uint8_t *s0, uint32_t sectors) {
    uint16_t u0 = rd16(s0), u1 = rd16(s0 + 2);
    if (u1 == 1 && u0 > 1 && u0 <= sectors)
        return AC1_TOC_COUNT_FIRST;
    return AC1_TOC_OFFSET_FIRST;
}

int ac1_mxt_open(ac1_mxt *m, const uint8_t *data, size_t size, ac1_toc_kind hint) {
    if (!m || !data || size < AC1_MXT_SECTOR || (size % AC1_MXT_SECTOR))
        return -1;
    memset(m, 0, sizeof *m);
    m->data = data;
    m->size = size;
    m->sectors = (uint32_t)(size / AC1_MXT_SECTOR);
    m->kind = (hint == AC1_TOC_AUTO) ? detect_kind(data, m->sectors) : hint;

    /* index of the first offset in the u16 table */
    uint32_t base = (m->kind == AC1_TOC_COUNT_FIRST) ? 1 : 0;
    uint32_t count = (m->kind == AC1_TOC_COUNT_FIRST) ? rd16(data) : 0;

    /* For offset-first, walk the leading monotonic run as offsets. */
    if (m->kind == AC1_TOC_OFFSET_FIRST) {
        uint32_t prev = 0, n = 0;
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 1024; i++) {
            uint16_t v = rd16(data + i * 2);
            if (v < prev || v > m->sectors) break;
            prev = v; n++;
        }
        count = (n > 0) ? n - 1 : 0;  /* last value is the end sentinel */
    }
    if (count == 0 || count > 1024) return -1;
    m->count = count;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i <= count; i++)
        m->offset[i] = rd16(data + (base + i) * 2);
    return 0;
}

int ac1_mxt_entry(const ac1_mxt *m, uint32_t i, size_t *off, size_t *len) {
    if (!m || i >= m->count) return -1;
    uint32_t s0 = m->offset[i], s1 = m->offset[i + 1];
    if (off) *off = (size_t)s0 * AC1_MXT_SECTOR;
    if (len) *len = (size_t)(s1 - s0) * AC1_MXT_SECTOR;
    return 0;
}

uint32_t ac1_mxt_checksum(const void *entry, size_t len) {
    const uint8_t *p = (const uint8_t *)entry;
    size_t nwords = len / 4;
    uint32_t sum = AC1_MXT_CHECKSUM_SEED;
    if (nwords == 0) return sum;
    for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < nwords; i++)   /* every word except the last */
        sum += rd32(p + i * 4);
    return sum;
}

int ac1_mxt_verify(const void *entry, size_t len) {
    size_t nwords = len / 4;
    if (nwords == 0) return 0;
    uint32_t stored = rd32((const uint8_t *)entry + (nwords - 1) * 4);
    return ac1_mxt_checksum(entry, len) == stored;
}

void ac1_mxt_fix_checksum(void *entry, size_t len) {
    size_t nwords = len / 4;
    if (nwords == 0) return;
    uint32_t cks = ac1_mxt_checksum(entry, len);
    uint8_t *w = (uint8_t *)entry + (nwords - 1) * 4;
    w[0] = (uint8_t)(cks);       w[1] = (uint8_t)(cks >> 8);
    w[2] = (uint8_t)(cks >> 16); w[3] = (uint8_t)(cks >> 24);
}

void ac1_overlay_read_header(const void *entry, ac1_overlay_header *h) {
    const uint8_t *p = (const uint8_t *)entry;
    h->flags    = rd32(p);
    h->entry_fn = rd32(p + 4);
    memcpy(h->magic, p + 8, 8);
}

```

`tools/README.md`:

```md
# AC1 RE tool belt (`tools/`)

Accelerators for the Armored Core 1 reverse-engineering workflow (the Farsi
localization mod's own build scripts live in `mods/farsi/`).
Run `tools/ghidra/setup_re_tools.sh` once on a new machine to install/verify everything.

## Where your files live (environment variables)
Nothing in the repo points at a fixed machine path. Scripts find the repo root from
their own location and take your local files from these variables:

| variable | meaning | default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AC1_BIN` | your pristine `SLUS-01323` v1.1 image (2352-B sectors) | *(required by `extract_fdat.py`, `build_filemap.py`, the Farsi bake)* |
| `AC1_RE_ROOT` | repo root, for Ghidra scripts run from a copied script dir | parent of `ghidra_scripts/` |
| `AC1_GHIDRA_PROJECT_DIR` | directory holding `AC_1_USA_2048_RE.gpr` | repo root |
| `M2C_DIR` | your m2c checkout (venv at `.venv`, POSIX `bin/` or Windows `Scripts/` layout) | `~/Applications/m2c` |
| `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` | unpacked Ghidra release (`ghidraRun[.bat]`, `support/analyzeHeadless[.bat]`) | *(unset → the Ubuntu snap paths)* |
| `GHIDRA_EXT_DIR` | Ghidra Extensions dir (where `ghidra_psx_ldr` goes) | `$GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR/Ghidra/Extensions` if that is set, else the snap's `~/snap/ghidra/…` user dir |
| `MIPS_PREFIX` | cross-toolchain prefix for `gcc`/`objdump`/`objcopy`/`nm`/`as`/`ld` | auto: `mipsel-linux-gnu-` (apt) if on PATH, else `mipsel-none-elf-` (PCSX-Redux prebuilt) |

The shell scripts share this resolution via `tools/ghidra/re_env.sh`; the Python
tools (`tools/re/disasm_batch.py`, `mods/farsi/build_rtl_patch.py`) apply the same rules.

### Windows note
Everything here runs under **Git Bash** (MSYS2); PowerShell/cmd are not supported.
- Toolchain: the PCSX-Redux prebuilt `mipsel-none-elf-*` GCC is picked up unrenamed
  once its `bin` is on PATH (or set `MIPS_PREFIX=mipsel-none-elf-` explicitly).
- Python: scripts call `python3` where it exists and fall back to `python`. The
  Microsoft Store `python3` stub shadows a real install — either disable it in
  *App execution aliases* or make a `python3.exe` copy next to `python.exe`.
- Ghidra: set `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` to the unpacked zip; the install-wide
  Extensions dir is `<install>\Ghidra\Extensions`, while Ghidra's per-user dir
  (settings, per-user extensions) lives at `%APPDATA%\ghidra\ghidra_<ver>_PUBLIC`.
- `ghidra_restart.sh` uses PowerShell `Stop-Process` instead of `pkill` and
  launches `ghidraRun.bat`; `ghidra_overlay.sh` runs `analyzeHeadless.bat`.

## `duckstation/` — save states
- **`states.py`** — the save-state **library**: `archive <slot> <id>` copies a
  DuckStation slot file into a directory outside the repo (`AC1_STATES_DIR`,
  default `~/dev/ac1_states`) under a stable ID, extracts the thumbnail, reads
  mission/stage/flags from RAM and appends a row to the committed manifest
  `disc_map/states/STATES.tsv`; `stage <id> <slot>` puts one back; `check`
  verifies sha256s; `list` queries. Slots are scratch, **docs cite IDs** — see
  `disc_map/states/README.md`. Test: `python tools/duckstation/states_test.py`.
- **`radio_line.py`** — plays one XA radio line in the running game through
  DuckStation's MCP server (sadnescity fork, port 2346) and measures what came out:
  stages a library state into a scratch slot with its media path rewritten to a
  disc copy's `.cue`, boots the copy, calls the game's XA line player
  `FUN_8004DB18(id)` from a breakpoint on `0x8005804C` with every register saved
  and restored, records with the `capture` tool and reports the normalised
  cross-correlation of the capture against the dubbed take and the pristine channel
  decodes (`docs/AUDIO_PIPELINE.md` §6). `--clip` takes a `voice_manifest.tsv` id,
  `--id` a raw `file_index << 4 | channel`; urllib only for the emulator part,
  `tools/audio/.venv` for the analysis (`--analyse-only` runs it on an existing MP4).
  ```
  tools/audio/.venv/Scripts/python tools/duckstation/radio_line.py --clip TALK00_ch12_c000 \
      --disc ~/dev/ac1_dub.cue --capture out/dub.mp4 --take take.wav \
      --shutdown --boot-after "${AC1_BIN%.bin}.cue" --load-after 3 --delete-slot
  ```
- **`savestate.py`** — offline DUCCS reader (header, RAM by PS1 address, VRAM,
  thumbnail, frame counter); `docs/SAVESTATE_FORMAT.md`. Needs a zstd decoder:
  `pip install zstandard` or the `zstd` CLI (neither ships with Windows).
- Extra variables: `AC1_STATES_DIR` (library), `AC1_DS_DIR` (DuckStation data dir,
  auto-detected from Documents/DuckStation or `~/.local/share/duckstation`),
  `AC1_DS_EXE` (emulator exe, for the build string). `AC1_BIN` supplies the EXE
  anchor + disc identity.

## `setup_re_tools.sh`
Idempotent installer + health report. Sets up m2c, checks the mipsel toolchain,
installs/verifies the Ghidra PSX loader + PSYQ signatures, and confirms the
overlay-import script. Safe to re-run; only fetches what's missing.

## `overlay2c.sh <hex_addr> <len> [binfile] [base]`  — the daily workhorse
Decompiles a slice of MIPS to C via `objdump` + **m2c**. The name/menu code lives
in a runtime overlay Ghidra's base project doesn't cover, so this turns a live
address range into readable C in one step.
```
tools/ghidra/overlay2c.sh 0x80082190 0x1b0          # decompile the name-input handler
```
- Default binfile = `overlay_80050000.bin` (RAM dump), base = `0x80050000`.
- To decompile freshly-patched live code, dump RAM first (DuckStation
  `read_memory` → file) and pass it as `binfile` with the right `base`.
- Internals: `objdump2m2c.py` converts objdump output to m2c GAS asm (branch
  targets → `.L` labels, `jal` → `func_<addr>`, `$`-prefixed regs). Out-of-slice
  branch targets get trailing stub labels + a WARNING (means `len` was too small
  — grow it to capture the whole function).
- m2c lives at your m2c install (e.g. `~/Applications/m2c`; venv at `.venv`).

**Validated** against hand-RE'd routines (cursor.update original `n*16+8`, the
name handler = `farsi_name_input.c`, `box_init` alloc `0x800501bc` + `+0x74`
update method). **Two caveats found doing so:**
- `overlay_80050000.bin` is a Jun-6 RAM dump → STALE for anything baked Jun-7
  (cursor RTL `0x80083a28`, `boxhook`/`cursext` are original/zeros in it), and it
  is not on this PC. The **current mission-overlay image** is the full 2 MB RAM dump
  `M30-ctrl-01__20261017.ram.bin` in the save-state library (`$AC1_STATES_DIR`,
  default `~/dev/ac1_states`): pristine disc, mission 30 live, so FDAT overlay 202
  is resident at `0x8004ADA0` and the objobj at `0x801C4B40`. Pass it with
  `base 0x80000000`:
  ```
  tools/ghidra/overlay2c.sh 0x8004F1A8 0x200 "$AC1_STATES_DIR/M30-ctrl-01__20261017.ram.bin" 0x80000000
  ```
  The same image can be regenerated from the archived state offline
  (`savestate.py <state> --dump-ram out.bin`). For freshly baked code, re-dump
  live RAM (DuckStation `read_memory` path=) on the relevant screen instead.
- m2c can't resolve `jr` **switch/jump tables** ("Unable to determine jump
  table") — decode a sub-range that avoids the dispatcher, or read those in
  Ghidra/live disasm.

## `ghidra_restart.sh`
Kills Ghidra (GUI + decompiler + headless), clears stale `.lock`/`.lock~` that
block reopening, and relaunches Ghidra (`$GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`, else the snap) with `AC_1_USA_2048_RE.gpr`. Does
NOT kill the GhidraMCP python bridge. After the window opens, double-click the
program so GhidraMCP serves on `:8080` (health: `curl :8080/list_functions`).

## `resurrect.sh [--go] [delay]`
Restarts THIS Claude Code session and resumes the same conversation (full
context) — used after building new MCP servers / Ghidra plugins / deferred tools
that need a fresh Claude to load. DRY-RUN by default; `--go` arms a detached
supervisor that waits `delay`s, opens a new terminal running
`claude --resume $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` in this repo, then kills the old
session. Needs `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` (Claude Code exports it).

## PSYQ signatures (auto-name SDK functions) — Ghidra, GUI step
`ghidra_psx_ldr` (installed in the Ghidra Extensions dir, see `GHIDRA_EXT_DIR`) ships PSYQ signature DBs
`psyq260…psyq470.gdt`. To label `libgpu`/`libgte`/`libcd`/`libapi` etc. in the
base exe: CodeBrowser → `Edit ▸ Options ▸ Program Information ▸ PsyQ Version`,
set the version, then re-run Auto Analysis with the PsyQ Signatures analyzer on.
AC1 is a Psy-Q title, so this turns many unnamed `FUN_*` into named SDK calls.

## Overlay → Ghidra (static decompile of overlay)
`ghidra_scripts/ImportAC1Overlay.py` maps `overlay_80050000.bin` in at
`0x80050000` and disassembles known entries, so the overlay becomes decompilable
via Ghidra + the MCP. Run it from the Ghidra Script Manager. (For one-off
functions, `overlay2c.sh` is faster.)
```

```
## jPSXdec (disc indexer + XA / STR decoder)
The disc map (`disc_map/disc_files.json`) and the voice pipeline both use
[jPSXdec](https://github.com/m35/jpsxdec) (Java; v2.x runs on the Temurin JDK 21 at
`JAVA_HOME`). Install once:

1. Download `jpsxdec_v2.1-beta.zip` from the official release page
   <https://github.com/m35/jpsxdec/releases/tag/v2.1> into its own empty folder
   (e.g. `~/dev/_dl/jpsxdec_v2.1/`).
2. Verify it against the release's digest (shown by
   `gh api repos/m35/jpsxdec/releases/latest --jq '.assets[0].digest'`):
   `sha256sum jpsxdec_v2.1-beta.zip` → `e11787a2…cd45b` for v2.1.
3. Unpack to `~/dev/jpsxdec/` (gives `~/dev/jpsxdec/jpsxdec_v2.1-beta/jpsxdec.jar`,
   plus `doc/jPSXdec-manual.pdf`). The audio scripts find it there; elsewhere set
   `JPSXDEC_JAR=/path/to/jpsxdec.jar`.

Handy commands (jPSXdec writes `index.log`/`save.log`/`debug00.log` into the cwd —
run it from a scratch dir, as the audio scripts do):
```
java -jar "$JPSXDEC_JAR" -f "$AC1_BIN" -x ac1.idx            # index the disc (~6 s)
java -jar "$JPSXDEC_JAR" -x ac1.idx -i "GG/BGM/TALK00.XA[3]" -af wav -dir out   # one XA channel
java -jar "$JPSXDEC_JAR" -x ac1.idx -i "GG/STR/ACED1.STR[0.0]" -af wav -dir out  # a video's audio
```
`tools/extract/build_filemap.py` turns such an index into `disc_files.json`.

## `audio/` — spoken voice lines → manifest → dub (`tools/audio/`)
Extracts the TALK XA channels and STR audio tracks with jPSXdec, splits them into
clips, transcribes them with faster-whisper (CPU), clusters speakers, matches the
text against the MIS.T corpus and writes `disc_map/voice_manifest.tsv` plus a local
review page. Full write-up: [`docs/AUDIO_PIPELINE.md`](../docs/AUDIO_PIPELINE.md).
```
tools/audio/setup_audio.sh                                   # venv + deps (once)
tools/audio/.venv/Scripts/python tools/audio/run_all.py      # end to end
tools/audio/.venv/Scripts/python tools/audio/audio_test.py   # unit tests
```
Needs `AC1_BIN`, `JAVA_HOME` (JDK 21) and jPSXdec (above). Decoded audio stays in
`disc_map/extracted/AUDIO/` (gitignored); only the manifest is committed.

**Re-injection** (`reinject_xa.py`, docs §6): writes a replacement WAV take into
one TALK channel of a *copy* of the disc, driven by a manifest row. Encodes to
4-bit XA-ADPCM with `xa_adpcm.py` (pure numpy: codec, Form 2 sector packing,
CD-ROM EDC), rewrites exactly the clip's sectors keeping the original subheaders,
refuses takes longer than the clip's sector budget, and can verify the result by
decoding the patched stream with jPSXdec.
```
tools/audio/.venv/Scripts/python tools/audio/reinject_xa.py --clip TALK05_ch00_c000 \
    --wav take.wav --image ~/dev/ac1_dub.bin --verify-jpsxdec     # copies $AC1_BIN -> --image first
tools/audio/.venv/Scripts/python tools/audio/reinject_test.py   # codec / EDC / packing tests, no disc
```
`--image` must never be the pristine image (the script refuses it); `--dry-run`
encodes and reports without writing, `--trim` cuts an over-long take.
```

`tools/VALIDATION.md`:

```md
# Tool belt validation report (2026-06-07)

Goal: confirm the new RE tool belt — chiefly `overlay2c.sh` (objdump + m2c
asm→C) — actually works, by re-deriving routines that were previously reverse
engineered **by hand** (live DuckStation disassembly) and checking the output
against the documented findings.

## Method

`tools/ghidra/overlay2c.sh <addr> <len>` carves the byte range out of
`overlay_80050000.bin` (base `0x80050000`), disassembles it with
`mipsel-linux-gnu-objdump`, converts to m2c GAS asm via `objdump2m2c.py`, and
decompiles with m2c. Each target below has an independently-known behaviour from
prior sessions (see `project_ac1_name_rtl_layout`, `farsi_name_input.c`,
`farsi_name_rtl.c`).

## Results — 3/3 reproduced

| Target | Addr | Expected (prior hand-RE) | overlay2c / m2c output | Verdict |
|--------|------|--------------------------|------------------------|---------|
| cursor.update (original) | `0x80083a28` | `cursor_X = n*16 + 8`, clamp to `7*16+8` at n==8; reads n via `0x7c(a0)->0x96` | `temp_a1 = arg0->unk7C->unk96; var_v0 = temp_a1*0x10; if(n==8) var_v0 = 7*0x10; arg0->unk48 = var_v0+8` | ✅ exact |
| name-input handler | `0x80082190` | `farsi_name_input.c`: edge-detect, `SELTAB[row*17+col]` @`0x8004c700`, append to `LOGBUF` @`0x8004c750`, reverse-copy to name buf, END→`draw_confirm(0x8005d8d4)` + state `0x8008240c` | identical structure (mode `unk19!=0x41`, SELTAB index `(unk1F*0x11)+unk1E+0x80050000-0x3900`, LOGBUF reverse, END branch) | ✅ exact |
| box_init (front) | `0x8005b648` | element alloc via `0x800501bc`; update method at `+0x74`; type at `+0xa` | `temp_v0 = func_800501bc(arg4); temp_v0->unk74 = 0x800507FC; temp_v0->unkA = 1; temp_v0->unk84/86 = args` | ✅ exact |

Byte-level cross-check: the dump's `cursor.update` ends in `0800e003 480082ac`,
which is byte-for-byte the documented **original** tail — confirming m2c read the
real bytes, not a misdecode.

## Caveats discovered (and how to handle them)

1. **The static dump is stale.** `overlay_80050000.bin` is a Jun-6 RAM snapshot.
   Routines patched/baked on Jun-7 do **not** appear in it:
   - `cursor.update` `0x80083a28` is still the **original LTR** version (the RTL
     `120−n*16` bake isn't there).
   - `cursext` `0x80082130` and `boxhook` `0x80082108` are **all zeros** (m2c
     correctly reported "no instructions" for `cursext`).
   The name handler `0x80082190` *is* present, so the dump straddles the bake
   history. **Fix:** for current/baked code, dump live RAM (DuckStation
   `read_memory` with `path=`) on the relevant screen and pass it to
   `overlay2c.sh` as `binfile` with the right `base`.

2. **m2c can't resolve `jr` jump/switch tables.** A dispatcher deeper in
   `box_init` triggered "Unable to determine jump table for jr instruction."
   This is an m2c limitation, not a pipeline bug. **Fix:** decode a sub-range
   that avoids the dispatcher, or read those functions in Ghidra / live disasm.

## Hardening applied during validation

`objdump2m2c.py` now tolerates an under-sized `len`: branch targets past the
decoded slice get trailing stub labels (with a delay slot) plus a stderr WARNING
naming the missing targets, instead of failing to parse. Grow `len` when you see
that warning to capture the whole function.

## Conclusion

The tool belt is proven against real prior work. `overlay2c.sh` is reliable for
reading overlay routines provided the input bytes are current (re-dump after
bakes). PSYQ signatures and the helper scripts (`ghidra_restart.sh`,
`resurrect.sh`, `setup_re_tools.sh`) are installed and self-tested; see
`tools/README.md`.

```

`tools/audio/ac1audio.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
ac1audio.py — shared helpers for the AC1 voice-line pipeline (tools/audio/).

Covers the bits every stage needs: where the local (never committed) audio
work dir is, how to find your disc / Java / jPSXdec, how to read a jPSXdec
.idx, and — the part that matters for re-injection — the XA sector arithmetic
that maps a PCM sample range back to the disc sectors it was decoded from.

XA-ADPCM facts used here (CD-ROM XA, Mode 2 Form 2, 2324-B payload):
  * one sector = 18 sound groups x 128 B; 4-bit coding packs 8 sound units of
    28 samples per group  -> 18*8*28 = 4032 samples per sector (mono),
    2016 sample-frames per sector (stereo); 8-bit coding halves both.
  * a stream's sectors are interleaved with the other channels of the same
    file: audio sector k of stream S lives at disc sector
        S.sector_first + k * S.stride
    (stride 16 for the mono TALK files, 8 for the stereo BGM / STR tracks).
  * jPSXdec's .idx lists each stream with its Sectors:first-last, Channel,
    Stereo?, Samples/Sec, Bits/Sample and Sector stride.

Nothing here reads the game disc except `disc_bin()` resolving its path.
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
FILEMAP = os.path.join(ROOT, "disc_map", "disc_files.json")
# Local work dir for decoded audio. Gitignored (disc_map/extracted/ is derived game data).
AUDIO_DIR = os.environ.get("AC1_AUDIO_DIR") or os.path.join(ROOT, "disc_map", "extracted", "AUDIO")

SECTOR_RAW = 2352
XA_RATE_DEFAULT = 37800

# jPSXdec defaults: a per-user unpacked release under ~/dev/jpsxdec (Windows RE box
# layout, see tools/README.md) or ~/Applications/jpsxdec (the Ubuntu layout).
JPSXDEC_SEARCH = [
    os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "dev", "jpsxdec", "*", "jpsxdec.jar"),
    os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "dev", "jpsxdec", "jpsxdec.jar"),
    os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "Applications", "jpsxdec", "*", "jpsxdec.jar"),
    os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "Applications", "jpsxdec", "jpsxdec.jar"),
]


def log(*a):
    print(*a, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


def ensure_dir(p):
    os.makedirs(p, exist_ok=True)
    return p


def load_json(p, default=None):
    if not os.path.exists(p):
        if default is not None:
            return default
        sys.exit(f"missing {p} — run the earlier pipeline stage first")
    with open(p, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)


def save_json(p, obj):
    ensure_dir(os.path.dirname(p))
    tmp = p + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(obj, f, indent=1)
    os.replace(tmp, p)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- local tools
def disc_bin(explicit=None):
    """Your disc image: --bin, else the filemap's source_bin if set locally, else $AC1_BIN.
    The committed disc_files.json carries no path (bring your own disc)."""
    if explicit:
        p = explicit
    else:
        p = None
        if os.path.exists(FILEMAP):
            with open(FILEMAP) as f:
                p = json.load(f).get("source_bin")
        p = p or os.environ.get("AC1_BIN")
    if not p or not os.path.exists(p):
        sys.exit("disc image not found: set AC1_BIN to your SLUS-01323 v1.1 .bin (or pass --bin)")
    return p


def find_java():
    """java from $JAVA_HOME/bin, else PATH. jPSXdec v2.x runs on Temurin 21."""
    jh = os.environ.get("JAVA_HOME")
    if jh:
        for exe in ("java.exe", "java"):
            p = os.path.join(jh, "bin", exe)
            if os.path.exists(p):
                return p
    p = shutil.which("java")
    if not p:
        sys.exit("java not found: set JAVA_HOME (JDK 21) or put java on PATH")
    return p


def find_jpsxdec(explicit=None):
    """jpsxdec.jar: --jar, else $JPSXDEC_JAR, else the usual unpacked-release spots."""
    cands = [explicit, os.environ.get("JPSXDEC_JAR")]
    for pat in JPSXDEC_SEARCH:
        cands += sorted(glob.glob(pat))
    for c in cands:
        if c and os.path.exists(c):
            return c
    sys.exit("jpsxdec.jar not found: set JPSXDEC_JAR (see tools/README.md § jPSXdec)")


def run(cmd, **kw):
    log("  $", " ".join(f'"{c}"' if " " in c else c for c in cmd))
    return subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, **kw)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- jPSXdec .idx
def parse_kv(line):
    """jPSXdec rows are pipe-delimited key:value (ID/Path may contain ':' and '/').
    Same rule as tools/extract/build_filemap.py."""
    d = {}
    for field in line.rstrip("\n").split("|"):
        if ":" in field:
            k, _, v = field.partition(":")
            d[k.strip()] = v.strip()
    return d


def parse_sectors(s):
    m = re.match(r"(\d+)-(\d+)", s or "")
    return (int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))) if m else (None, None)


def parse_idx(path):
    """Return the list of item dicts from a jPSXdec .idx (each with idx/id/type/
    sector_first/sector_last plus the raw key:value fields)."""
    items = []
    with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as f:
        for raw in f:
            if not raw.startswith("#:"):
                continue
            kv = parse_kv(raw)
            first, last = parse_sectors(kv.get("Sectors"))
            items.append({
                "idx": int(kv.get("#", -1)),
                "id": kv.get("ID", ""),
                "type": kv.get("Type", ""),
                "sector_first": first,
                "sector_last": last,
                "raw": kv,
            })
    return items


def build_index(bin_path, idx_path, jar=None, java=None):
    """java -jar jpsxdec.jar -f <bin> -x <idx>  (about 6 s for the AC1 disc)."""
    java = java or find_java()
    jar = jar or find_jpsxdec()
    ensure_dir(os.path.dirname(idx_path))
    # cwd = the work dir: jPSXdec writes index.log / save.log / debug00.log into cwd
    run([java, "-jar", jar, "-f", bin_path, "-x", os.path.abspath(idx_path)],
        cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(idx_path)))
    if not os.path.exists(idx_path):
        sys.exit("jPSXdec did not write the index")
    return idx_path


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- XA streams
class XAStream:
    """One interleaved XA channel stream as jPSXdec indexes it.

    sector_first/sector_last are inclusive DISC sectors of the first/last audio
    sector of this stream; audio sector k sits at sector_first + k*stride.
    """

    def __init__(self, id, sector_first, sector_last, stride, channel=0,
                 stereo=False, rate=XA_RATE_DEFAULT, bits=4):
        self.id = id
        self.sector_first = int(sector_first)
        self.sector_last = int(sector_last)
        self.stride = int(stride)
        self.channel = int(channel)
        self.stereo = bool(stereo)
        self.rate = int(rate)
        self.bits = int(bits)
        span = self.sector_last - self.sector_first
        if span < 0 or span % self.stride:
            raise ValueError(f"{id}: sector span {span} not a multiple of stride {self.stride}")

    @classmethod
    def from_idx_item(cls, it):
        kv = it["raw"]
        return cls(it["id"], it["sector_first"], it["sector_last"],
                   kv.get("Sector stride", 1), kv.get("Channel", 0),
                   kv.get("Stereo?", "No") == "Yes", kv.get("Samples/Sec", XA_RATE_DEFAULT),
                   kv.get("Bits/Sample", 4))

    # --- sizes
    @property
    def n_sectors(self):
        return (self.sector_last - self.sector_first) // self.stride + 1

    @property
    def samples_per_sector(self):
        """PCM sample-frames decoded from one audio sector."""
        per = 4032 if self.bits == 4 else 2016
        return per // (2 if self.stereo else 1)

    @property
    def total_samples(self):
        return self.n_sectors * self.samples_per_sector

    @property
    def duration_s(self):
        return self.total_samples / self.rate

    # --- mapping
    def sector_of_sample(self, sample):
        """Disc sector holding sample-frame `sample` (0-based within the stream)."""
        if sample < 0 or sample >= self.total_samples:
            raise ValueError(f"sample {sample} outside stream of {self.total_samples}")
        return self.sector_first + (sample // self.samples_per_sector) * self.stride

    def audio_sector_index(self, sample):
        return sample // self.samples_per_sector

    def sector_range(self, start, end):
        """Inclusive disc-sector range covering sample-frames [start, end)."""
        if end <= start:
            raise ValueError("empty range")
        return (self.sector_of_sample(start), self.sector_of_sample(end - 1))

    def sample_range_of_sector(self, sector):
        """[start, end) sample-frames decoded from disc sector `sector`."""
        off = sector - self.sector_first
        if off < 0 or off % self.stride or sector > self.sector_last:
            raise ValueError(f"sector {sector} not in stream {self.id}")
        k = off // self.stride
        return (k * self.samples_per_sector, (k + 1) * self.samples_per_sector)

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "id": self.id, "sector_first": self.sector_first, "sector_last": self.sector_last,
            "stride": self.stride, "channel": self.channel, "stereo": self.stereo,
            "rate": self.rate, "bits": self.bits, "n_sectors": self.n_sectors,
            "samples_per_sector": self.samples_per_sector, "total_samples": self.total_samples,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d):
        return cls(d["id"], d["sector_first"], d["sector_last"], d["stride"], d["channel"],
                   d["stereo"], d["rate"], d["bits"])


def is_talk_item(it):
    return it["type"] == "XA" and re.match(r"GG/BGM/TALK\d\d\.XA\[\d+\]$", it["id"]) is not None


def is_str_audio_item(it):
    # jPSXdec v2.1 lists a video's audio as a child XA item: GG/STR/ACED1.STR[0.0]
    return it["type"] == "XA" and re.match(r"GG/STR/[A-Z0-9]+\.STR\[\d+\.\d+\]$", it["id"]) is not None


def stream_short_name(item_id):
    """GG/BGM/TALK03.XA[12] -> TALK03_ch12 ; GG/STR/ACED1.STR[0.0] -> ACED1_str"""
    m = re.match(r"GG/BGM/(TALK\d\d)\.XA\[(\d+)\]$", item_id)
    if m:
        return f"{m.group(1)}_ch{int(m.group(2)):02d}"
    m = re.match(r"GG/STR/([A-Z0-9]+)\.STR\[\d+\.\d+\]$", item_id)
    if m:
        return f"{m.group(1)}_str"
    return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", item_id).strip("_")


def source_kind(item_id):
    return "TALK" if "/TALK" in item_id else ("STR" if ".STR[" in item_id else "XA")
```

`tools/audio/audio_test.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
audio_test.py — unit tests for the voice pipeline's bookkeeping.

Covers the two pieces that must be right for re-injection to be possible later:
  * ac1audio.XAStream — sample <-> disc-sector arithmetic for interleaved XA
    streams (mono stride-16 TALK channels, stereo stride-8 STR tracks), and the
    jPSXdec .idx parser that feeds it;
  * split_utterances.split_by_energy — the silence splitter, on synthetic audio.

Needs only numpy (the tools/audio/.venv has it). No game data is read.
  tools/audio/.venv/Scripts/python tools/audio/audio_test.py
"""
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import ac1audio as A  # noqa: E402
from split_utterances import split_by_energy  # noqa: E402

RATE = 37800

IDX_SAMPLE = """\
; jPSXdec index sample (two streams + one video, as v2.1 writes them)
Filename:fake.bin|Sector size:2352|Sector count:100|First sector offset:0
[Index]
#:226|ID:GG/BGM/TALK00.XA|Sectors:60284-62971|Type:File|Size:5505024|Path:GG/BGM/TALK00.XA|Has mode 2 form 2:Yes|Has CD audio:No
#:227|ID:GG/BGM/TALK00.XA[0]|Sectors:60284-60908|Type:XA|File:1|Channel:0|Stereo?:No|Samples/Sec:37800|Bits/Sample:4|Sector stride:16|Disc speed:2x
#:2591|ID:GG/STR/ACED5.STR[0]|Sectors:155981-157931|Type:Video|Dimensions:320x240|Frame Count:390
#:2592|ID:GG/STR/ACED5.STR[0.0]|Sectors:155988-157788|Type:XA|File:1|Channel:1|Stereo?:Yes|Samples/Sec:37800|Bits/Sample:4|Sector stride:8|Disc speed:2x
"""


class XAStreamMath(unittest.TestCase):
    def talk(self):
        # GG/BGM/TALK05.XA[0] as indexed: 8 audio sectors, stride 16, mono 4-bit
        return A.XAStream("GG/BGM/TALK05.XA[0]", 71740, 71852, 16, channel=0, stereo=False)

    def test_sizes_mono(self):
        s = self.talk()
        self.assertEqual(s.n_sectors, 8)
        self.assertEqual(s.samples_per_sector, 4032)
        self.assertEqual(s.total_samples, 32256)  # == what jPSXdec decodes for this item
        self.assertAlmostEqual(s.duration_s, 32256 / 37800)

    def test_sizes_stereo(self):
        s = A.XAStream("GG/STR/ACED5.STR[0.0]", 155988, 157788, 8, channel=1, stereo=True)
        self.assertEqual(s.n_sectors, 226)
        self.assertEqual(s.samples_per_sector, 2016)
        self.assertEqual(s.total_samples, 226 * 2016)

    def test_eight_bit(self):
        s = A.XAStream("x", 100, 116, 16, stereo=False, bits=8)
        self.assertEqual(s.samples_per_sector, 2016)
        s = A.XAStream("x", 100, 116, 16, stereo=True, bits=8)
        self.assertEqual(s.samples_per_sector, 1008)

    def test_sector_of_sample(self):
        s = self.talk()
        self.assertEqual(s.sector_of_sample(0), 71740)
        self.assertEqual(s.sector_of_sample(4031), 71740)
        self.assertEqual(s.sector_of_sample(4032), 71756)      # next audio sector = +stride
        self.assertEqual(s.sector_of_sample(32255), 71852)     # last sample -> sector_last
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            s.sector_of_sample(32256)

    def test_sector_range_and_inverse(self):
        s = self.talk()
        self.assertEqual(s.sector_range(0, 4032), (71740, 71740))
        self.assertEqual(s.sector_range(4000, 4100), (71740, 71756))  # straddles a boundary
        self.assertEqual(s.sector_range(8064, 32256), (71772, 71852))
        self.assertEqual(s.sample_range_of_sector(71756), (4032, 8064))
        self.assertEqual(s.audio_sector_index(8063), 1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            s.sample_range_of_sector(71757)  # not on the stride grid
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            s.sector_range(10, 10)

    def test_every_sample_round_trips(self):
        s = A.XAStream("x", 1000, 1000 + 16 * 4, 16)
        for smp in range(0, s.total_samples, 97):
            sec = s.sector_of_sample(smp)
            a, b = s.sample_range_of_sector(sec)
            self.assertTrue(a <= smp < b)

    def test_bad_span_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            A.XAStream("x", 100, 109, 16)

    def test_dict_round_trip(self):
        s = A.XAStream("GG/STR/ACED5.STR[0.0]", 155988, 157788, 8, channel=1, stereo=True)
        d = s.to_dict()
        t = A.XAStream.from_dict(d)
        self.assertEqual(t.to_dict(), d)
        self.assertTrue(d["stereo"])


class IdxParsing(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_parse_and_classify(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            p = os.path.join(td, "t.idx")
            with open(p, "w") as f:
                f.write(IDX_SAMPLE)
            items = A.parse_idx(p)
        self.assertEqual([it["idx"] for it in items], [226, 227, 2591, 2592])
        talk = [it for it in items if A.is_talk_item(it)]
        strs = [it for it in items if A.is_str_audio_item(it)]
        self.assertEqual([t["id"] for t in talk], ["GG/BGM/TALK00.XA[0]"])
        self.assertEqual([t["id"] for t in strs], ["GG/STR/ACED5.STR[0.0]"])
        st = A.XAStream.from_idx_item(talk[0])
        self.assertEqual((st.sector_first, st.sector_last, st.stride, st.stereo, st.rate),
                         (60284, 60908, 16, False, 37800))
        self.assertEqual(st.n_sectors, 40)
        st2 = A.XAStream.from_idx_item(strs[0])
        self.assertTrue(st2.stereo)
        self.assertEqual(st2.stride, 8)

    def test_short_names(self):
        self.assertEqual(A.stream_short_name("GG/BGM/TALK03.XA[12]"), "TALK03_ch12")
        self.assertEqual(A.stream_short_name("GG/STR/ACED1.STR[0.0]"), "ACED1_str")
        self.assertEqual(A.source_kind("GG/BGM/TALK03.XA[12]"), "TALK")
        self.assertEqual(A.source_kind("GG/STR/ACED1.STR[0.0]"), "STR")


def burst(t0, t1, level_db=-12.0, seed=0):
    """White-noise burst spanning [t0, t1) seconds at the given RMS level."""
    n = int((t1 - t0) * RATE)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    y = rng.standard_normal(n).astype(np.float32)
    return int(t0 * RATE), y / (np.sqrt((y ** 2).mean()) + 1e-9) * 10 ** (level_db / 20)


def build(total_s, bursts):
    x = np.zeros(int(total_s * RATE), dtype=np.float32)
    for t0, t1, lvl in bursts:
        s, y = burst(t0, t1, lvl, seed=int(t0 * 1000))
        x[s:s + len(y)] += y
    return x


class SilenceSplitter(unittest.TestCase):
    TOL = int(0.15 * RATE)  # 100 ms pad + one 20 ms window + hop slop

    def test_three_utterances_over_digital_silence(self):
        x = build(6.0, [(0.5, 1.5, -12), (2.5, 2.9, -15), (4.0, 5.2, -10)])
        spans = split_by_energy(x, RATE)
        self.assertEqual(len(spans), 3)
        for (s, e), (t0, t1, _) in zip(spans, [(0.5, 1.5, 0), (2.5, 2.9, 0), (4.0, 5.2, 0)]):
            self.assertLessEqual(abs(s - int(t0 * RATE)), self.TOL)
            self.assertLessEqual(abs(e - int(t1 * RATE)), self.TOL)
            self.assertLess(s, e)

    def test_short_blip_dropped_and_small_gap_bridged(self):
        # 50 ms click: below min_speech_ms -> dropped. Two bursts 150 ms apart: one clip.
        x = build(5.0, [(0.5, 0.55, -12), (2.0, 2.6, -12), (2.75, 3.3, -12)])
        spans = split_by_energy(x, RATE, min_speech_ms=150, min_gap_ms=350)
        self.assertEqual(len(spans), 1)
        s, e = spans[0]
        self.assertLessEqual(abs(s - int(2.0 * RATE)), self.TOL)
        self.assertLessEqual(abs(e - int(3.3 * RATE)), self.TOL)

    def test_gap_longer_than_min_gap_splits(self):
        x = build(5.0, [(1.0, 1.6, -12), (2.1, 2.7, -12)])  # 500 ms apart
        self.assertEqual(len(split_by_energy(x, RATE, min_gap_ms=350)), 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(split_by_energy(x, RATE, min_gap_ms=700)), 1)

    def test_low_noise_floor_does_not_trigger(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
        x = (rng.standard_normal(3 * RATE) * 10 ** (-60 / 20)).astype(np.float32)  # -60 dBFS hiss
        self.assertEqual(split_by_energy(x, RATE), [])
        x[RATE:2 * RATE] += burst(1.0, 2.0, -20)[1]
        self.assertEqual(len(split_by_energy(x, RATE)), 1)

    def test_runs_to_end_and_clamps(self):
        x = build(2.0, [(1.5, 2.0, -12)])
        spans = split_by_energy(x, RATE)
        self.assertEqual(len(spans), 1)
        self.assertEqual(spans[0][1], len(x))
        self.assertGreaterEqual(spans[0][0], 0)

    def test_empty_and_silent(self):
        self.assertEqual(split_by_energy(np.zeros(0, np.float32), RATE), [])
        self.assertEqual(split_by_energy(np.zeros(RATE, np.float32), RATE), [])

    def test_stereo_input_downmixed(self):
        mono = build(3.0, [(1.0, 2.0, -12)])
        stereo = np.stack([mono, mono * 0.5], axis=1)
        self.assertEqual(len(split_by_energy(stereo, RATE)), 1)

    def test_clip_sectors_follow_from_samples(self):
        # Splitter output feeds XAStream.sector_range: a 1 s clip at 0.5 s in a
        # TALK channel covers audio sectors 4..14 -> disc sectors first+4*16..first+14*16
        st = A.XAStream("GG/BGM/TALK00.XA[3]", 60287, 60287 + 16 * 60, 16, channel=3)
        x = build(3.0, [(0.5, 1.5, -12)])
        (s, e), = split_by_energy(x, RATE)
        a, b = st.sector_range(s, e)
        self.assertEqual(a, 60287 + (s // 4032) * 16)
        self.assertEqual(b, 60287 + ((e - 1) // 4032) * 16)
        self.assertEqual((a - 60287) % 16, 0)
        self.assertEqual((b - 60287) % 16, 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=1)
```
